witnesses.title: Notebook document semantics: stable cell id vs display order vs execution order
witnesses.label: executed by candidate
witnesses.input: In-memory notebook dict with three code cells (ids cell-01..03, execution_counts 1..3, one execute_result output bound to execution_count 2), built to the v4.5 schema constraints from source S1; the check reverses the cells array and re-validates identity/order/association invariants with assertions (stdlib re only).
witnesses.expected_behavior: Cell ids remain valid and stable after reordering; execution order (execution_count) is independent of display order; the saved execute_result stays associated with its producing execution; unexecuted cell has execution_count null; error outputs are structured (ename/evalue/traceback).
witnesses.justification: Each expectation is a direct restatement of the captured nbformat v4.5 schema text (S1 locator fields); the check validates that a downstream tracker can rely on these invariants, not that the nbformat library validates.

observed.stdout_summary: W1 PASS; display order after edit ['cell-03','cell-02','cell-01']; execution order ['cell-01','cell-02','cell-03']; output->execution association stable; null ec + structured error output OK

witnesses.scope_limits: Isolated component check on synthetic dict data; does not execute nbformat/ipykernel or prove any editor product behavior; the v4.5 schema was captured from a floating main branch (S1 limit).

witnesses.title: Output-status / invalidation state machine (current/stale/failed/unverified)
witnesses.label: executed by candidate
witnesses.input: Candidate-designed rule set over a linear notebook A->B->C with the six invalidation rules R1..R6 (upstream cell edit, dataset/env edit, kernel restart, interrupted run, clean replay incl. error path); pure stdlib dict logic, assertions on full state dictionaries.
witnesses.expected_behavior: R1 editing A stales A,B,C and rerunning only A leaves B,C stale; R2/R3 dataset or env edits stale all current outputs; R4 restart turns every 'current' into 'unverified' while 'failed' stays failed; R5 a cancelled run marks mid-flight cells 'unverified' (never 'current'); R6 replay marks completed cells 'current', an erroring cell 'failed', and its downstream 'unverified'.
witnesses.justification: These rules operationalize the brief's requirements (invalidation effects; restart/interrupt must not silently label old outputs current) using the cell-id/output-association mechanisms evidenced by S1/S4/S5; the check proves the rule set is internally consistent and complete for the tested transitions.

observed.stdout_summary: W2 PASS; all six rules' resulting state dictionaries printed

attempt_history.cause: candidate harness bug (rev 1 asserted the boolean return of the error-path replay step, which is False by design); rule logic unchanged in rev 2

witnesses.scope_limits: Isolated component check of candidate logic on a 3-cell linear graph; no kernel, no real upstream/downstream analysis (transitive dependencies beyond a linear chain are design work, UNEXECUTED); does not prove a real replay engine implements these rules.

witnesses.title: Bounded streaming ingestion with reject capture, no source mutation, and preview-vs-full-dataset separation
witnesses.label: executed by candidate
witnesses.input: data = {rows: 20000, chunk_hint_bytes: 16384, preview_n: 100}. Candidate-authored code writes a synthetic CSV (unicode labels, empty-string missing values, timestamps, one field-count-violating line at row 13335, upward value trend), then re-reads it with a chunked streaming loop (16 KB read hints), captures malformed lines into a reject ledger with line numbers, accumulates full-dataset vs first-100-row value means, and hashes the source before/after.
witnesses.expected_behavior: ok_count + rejected_count == total rows (no silent drops); exactly one reject recorded with the correct line number; source file SHA-256 unchanged; preview mean materially differs from the full mean (gap > 0.2), demonstrating a bounded preview cannot be presented as a full-dataset property; the loop buffers a bounded number of lines per chunk.
witnesses.justification: Reject-ledger semantics mirror the documented DuckDB store_rejects pattern (S8); no-mutation and preview-separation are explicit brief requirements; the trend fixture makes the preview-vs-full gap deterministic rather than probabilistic.

observed.stdout_summary: W3 PASS; total=20000 ok=19999 rejected=1 (line 13335, field_count!=4); source sha256 unchanged; full mean=1.0000 (n=17141) vs 100-row preview mean=0.5029, gap=0.4970; max 417 lines buffered per chunk

attempt_history.cause: rev 1: the sandbox delivered the data parameter as a JSON string; rev 2+ parse defensively
rev 2: OSError Errno 27 'File too large' writing the 150k-row fixture — the isolated sandbox enforces a small per-file quota; fixture reduced to 20k rows (rev 3)

witnesses.scope_limits: Isolated component check with 20k-row synthetic data and a plain chunked reader (not pyarrow/DuckDB); it demonstrates contract mechanics, NOT 5 GB performance, NOT columnar-engine behavior, and NOT memory-profile compliance of any real engine (explicitly UNEXECUTED at 5 GB scale).
